description:
Maintainer's architecture direction, 2026-08-04: 'OutramFoam driftflux and 6 eqn models have already been ported in. These are to be introduced into Tampines.'

Already ported and available in crates/outram-foam-multiphase/src/:
  drift_flux.rs        -- drift-flux model
  two_fluid.rs         -- two-fluid (6-equation) model
  two_fluid_pimple.rs  -- its PIMPLE loop
  pimple.rs, wall_boiling.rs, chf.rs, dryout.rs

Task: introduce these into tampines as higher-fidelity options ABOVE the HEM baseline (see the sibling TampinesSteamArray bead), so a component can be run at HEM, drift-flux, or full two-fluid fidelity.

Design constraint (workspace rule): the fidelity choice is a CLOSED set, so it is enum dispatch -- never Box<dyn>/trait objects. A trait may still be used as a compile-time contract on each concrete model.

Cross-reference: the existing op-dt3.12/.13/.14/.15/.16 beads already track reduced 1D drift-flux / two-fluid / CHF / dryout / post-dryout for tampines -- check for overlap and either wire dependencies or close the duplicates rather than doing the work twice.

Note outram-foam-multiphase is a scaffold with no human V&V; anything adopted here needs V&V documenting methodology AND measured results per the workspace rule.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
SEQUENCING (maintainer, 2026-08-04): 'the 1D versions of drift flux and 6 eqn are to be the bread and butter of tampines before the AI is in... Before PINNs and other AI accelerations of the solver are in.'

So the 1D REDUCED models are the primary deliverable, not the full 3D CFD ports. Those already have beads: op-dt3.12 (1D Drift Flux), op-dt3.13 (1D Two-Fluid), op-dt3.14 (1D CHF), op-dt3.15 (1D Dryout), op-dt3.16 (1D Post-Dryout). This bead is the umbrella that says where the physics comes FROM (outram-foam-multiphase) and that it sits above the HEM baseline (op-dt3.18).

Order: HEM baseline (op-dt3.18) -> 1D drift-flux + 1D 6-eqn (op-dt3.12/.13) as the workhorse solvers -> only THEN PINNs / AI acceleration. The 'AI' in the TAMPINES acronym is explicitly a LATER stage; the deterministic 1D solvers must be the trustworthy baseline it is measured against first.

title: tampines: adopt OutramFoam drift-flux and two-fluid (6-eqn) models above the HEM baseline

description:
The gate that makes the rest of `op-yvj.4` trustworthy. Blocked by every
kernel bead; nothing in the epic may be described as working until this passes.

**Parity gate.** For every kernel added under this epic, a test that runs the
same problem through `Serial`, `CpuMulti`, and `Gpu` and compares:

- `Serial` vs `CpuMulti` should agree to near machine precision **unless** a
  reduction reorders summation — in which case say so and use a stated
  tolerance, do not just widen it silently.
- `Serial` vs `Gpu` needs an explicit tolerance justified by the precision the
  kernel actually runs at. **Do not assume f64 on the GPU** — many adapters
  give f32 for compute, and f32 accuracy across a full parameter range is
  already an open human-review question elsewhere in this workspace
  (`op-0nh`, Faddeeva). State the precision and the measured error, per kernel.
- For iterative solvers, compare **residual histories and iteration counts**,
  not just the final answer. A changed preconditioner shows up as a different
  iteration count long before it shows up as a wrong answer.

**Benchmarks.** Measure, do not assert, that the GPU path is actually faster:
report the crossover problem size per kernel, including the host-device
transfer, and record the hardware it was measured on. If a kernel never beats
`CpuMulti` at realistic sizes, that is a legitimate result — write it down and
leave the kernel off the auto-select policy rather than shipping a slower
default.

**Documentation** (workspace V&V rule — methodology *and* results): each gate's
doc comment states what is computed, the reference, the inputs, the pass
criterion, and then the actual measured numbers with the date and the hardware.

**No human V&V is claimed by any of this.** These are automated verification
gates written by an AI-assisted draft process; the crate README's
`## Bookkeeping status` axes stay ❌ until the maintainer personally signs off.

CI note: GPU tests must skip cleanly (not fail) on a host with no adapter, and
must not run at all on Android/Termux.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 on the GPU is ACCEPTED for now. Do not block this epic on f64 GPU support or on the op-0nh Faddeeva f32 accuracy review. Requirement is a DOCUMENTED CAVEAT, not a fix: every GPU kernel's doc comment must state (a) the precision it actually runs at, (b) the measured max/RMS deviation from the f64 serial CPU oracle on the stated test problem, and (c) that the GPU path is therefore not the reference result. The parity-gate tolerances are set to pass at f32 deliberately -- that is the maintainer's call, not a loosened tolerance of convenience. Iterative solvers keep the stricter check: a changed ITERATION COUNT or residual history is a real defect even at f32, and must not be waved through as precision noise. Revisit if a validation case is ever gated on GPU output.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVER for the field-algebra kernels (fields::parallel), 2026-08-12, 4 logical cores, --release --features parallel.

FINDING: compute::CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS = 4096 is FAR TOO LOW for these kernels. It is a placeholder I wrote without measurement, and measuring it shows it would make callers SLOWER, not faster.

c = a + b, best of 9 after 2 warm-ups, --test-threads=1, least-contended of 10 sweeps:

  n          serial      CpuMulti    speedup
  1024       0.43 us     7.59 us     0.06x
  4096       1.89 us     11.07 us    0.17x   <-- at the current placeholder: ~6x SLOWER
  16384      5.99 us     23.11 us    0.26x
  65536      56.27 us    30.39 us    1.85x
  131072     117.77 us   49.87 us    2.36x
  262144     239.65 us   89.52 us    2.68x
  1048576    2001.64 us  437.34 us   4.58x

Cause: these kernels are memory-bandwidth bound at 1-2 flops/element, so thread overhead dominates far longer than for compute-dense work.

THE CROSSOVER IS A BAND, NOT A POINT. Shared virtualised host: serial repeatable to <5%, parallel varies up to 4x run to run. Win counts over 10 sweeps: <=16384 -> 0/10; 65536 -> 4/10; 131072 -> 6/10; 262144 -> 9/10; 1048576 -> 10/10. Honest statement: crossover lies between 65536 and 262144 on this host and cannot be pinned further.

fields::parallel::field_parallel_crossover() therefore overrides the global constant at 131072 (majority winner), using the override mechanism compute.rs's own docs sanction. Losing at 131072 costs tens of microseconds; setting 262144 would forfeit a measured 1.3x-2.4x.

CAVEAT: one shared virtualised 4-core sandbox. Re-measure on real hardware before trusting 131072.

Kernel speedups at n=1048576 (representative of 4 runs): add 2.75x, axpy 2.49x, pointwise_mul 3.82x, sum 2.95x, l2_norm 2.70x, dot 2.56x, axpy_assign 3.23x. Range across runs 2.5x-4.3x.

REDUCTION DETERMINISM (relevant to this bead's parity-gate criteria): fixed-chunk tree reduction, REDUCTION_CHUNK=4096, chunks summed in index order. Bit-reproducible run to run (32/32 identical) AND identical across thread counts (pools of 1,2,3,4,7,8 all bitwise equal). NOT bit-equal to Serial: measured worst-case relative deviation 7.857e-14 (vol_integral); sum 5.690e-14, dot 7.189e-15, l2_norm 6.785e-15. Asserted tolerance 1e-11. min/max ARE bit-identical to serial. Element-wise kernels are bit-identical to Serial on every backend and size.

GPU: no field kernel exists; ComputeBackend::Gpu routes to the best CPU path, documented rather than silently pretended. The Serial-vs-Gpu half of this bead's parity gate is therefore still entirely open for this module.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVERS for the LDU kernels (ldu_matrix::parallel), 2026-08-12, available_parallelism()=4, release --features parallel, idle machine.

HEADLINE: there must NOT be one crate-wide CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS. The two kernel families measured so far want thresholds 64x apart, and a single number is wrong for at least one of them.

SpMV, time per call, best of 7 samples, two independent runs:

  cells     serial      CpuMulti    speedup   repeat
  1000      20.24 us    20.08 us    1.01x     1.00x
  1728      34.55 us    63.28 us    0.55x     0.65x
  2744      55.67 us    69.32 us    0.80x     1.21x
  4096      83.67 us    80.61 us    1.04x     1.02x   <-- break-even
  8000      165.60 us   114.06 us   1.45x     2.02x
  32768     690.40 us   277.86 us   2.48x     2.03x
  512000    13338 us    4822 us     2.77x     3.48x

For SpMV the placeholder 4096 is CORRECT -- it is precisely where the parallel path stops losing. SPMV_MIN_CELLS = 4096.

For vector ops 4096 is badly wrong: dot only wins from ~65536; axpy is still break-even at 262144 (1.87x one run, 1.00x the other) and reliable only from ~1048576. At 4096 elements axpy on 4 threads is 0.05x -- TWENTY TIMES SLOWER. VECOP_MIN_ELEMENTS = 262144.

Compare the field-algebra measurement already filed on this bead: those memory-bound kernels wanted 131072. So three kernel families, three different answers (4096 / 131072 / 262144). The right resolution for this bead is per-kernel measured constants with compute.rs's global as a floor, not a single tuned number.

THREAD SCALING, 262144 cells: 1 -> 6487 us, 2 -> 3481 us (1.86x), 4 -> 2322 us (2.79x), 8 -> 1830 us (3.54x). Output asserted BITWISE IDENTICAL at every thread count. The >3x on 4 cores is superlinear and reproducible; a cache hypothesis is documented in the code and explicitly labelled UNCONFIRMED.

PARITY (this bead's Serial-vs-CpuMulti criterion): spmv, residual, diagonal_reciprocal and axpy are BIT-FOR-BIT IDENTICAL to the serial path, not merely within tolerance -- the cell-gather stores each cell's incident faces in ascending face index, which is the order the serial scatter reaches them. Verified via to_bits() at 24/512/32768 cells, symmetric and asymmetric, at 1/2/4/8 threads. Reductions are bitwise identical across backends and thread counts but not equal to the flat krylov::vecops sums: dot worst 2.3744e-13 raw at n=4194304 (7.9476e-17 scaled by sum|a_i b_i|; the raw figure inflates because the test vectors cancel to ~150), normalised_residual 7.6520e-15 (~34 ulp), norm_l1 8.9257e-14, norm_l2 2.4996e-15.

Serial-vs-Gpu parity remains ENTIRELY OPEN for this module: there is no GPU LDU kernel, and ComputeBackend::Gpu degrades to the best CPU path (asserted in a test so it cannot silently claim the GPU).

CAVEATS: one machine, 4 cores, idle. Not measured on Android hardware or a many-core server. Under load the SpMV break-even moves right -- an earlier contended run put 4096 cells at 0.72x. norm_l1/norm_l2 were not separately benchmarked; they inherit dot's floor by assumption.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVER for batched root finding (math::parallel), 2026-08-12, available_parallelism()=4, release --features parallel, idle, best of 7, two independent runs.

This is the FOURTH kernel family measured and it moves in the OPPOSITE direction to the field kernels: 256, i.e. 16x BELOW the CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS placeholder of 4096, because root finding is compute-dense per lane where field algebra is memory-bound.

Iterative solve, wall clock per whole batch (cheap residual | costly residual):

  problems   serial      multi       speedup      serial      multi       speedup
  64         12.99 us    45.16 us    0.29x        42.85 us    62.99 us    0.68x
  128        25.96 us    57.24 us    0.45x        84.88 us    86.65 us    0.98x
  256        52.94 us    42.79 us    1.24x        175.37 us   126.70 us   1.38x   <-- crossover
  1024       201.83 us   127.52 us   1.58x        695.26 us   284.70 us   2.44x
  65536      13730.89 us 5071.05 us  2.71x        45778.24 us 16260.96 us 2.82x

ROOT_BATCH_MIN_PROBLEMS = 256, the smallest size at which neither closure lost in either run. Closed-form cubics cross at 1024 (POLY_ROOTS_MIN_EQUATIONS); at 256 the two paths are exactly break-even because POLY_BLOCK is 256 and rayon never splits. Per-lane costs are comparable (~153 ns/cubic vs ~209 ns/cheap iterative lane), so the 4x gap between those two constants is a conservative reading of a noisy shallow break-even, NOT a structural claim.

RUNNING TALLY for this bead: 256 (root finding) / 4096 (LDU SpMV) / 131072 (field algebra) / 262144 (LDU vecops). A 1024x spread, with the crate-wide placeholder sitting in the middle and wrong at both ends.

AND A HARDER PROBLEM FOR THIS BEAD: the iterative root-finding crossover depends on the CALLER'S RESIDUAL COST, which the crate cannot know -- the cheap and costly closures above differ by roughly 3.3x in serial time with identical kernel code. So 'measure the crossover per kernel' is not sufficient for this family; the constant is a default, and a caller with an expensive residual should override it. Worth deciding, for this bead, whether the API should let a caller supply a measured threshold rather than inheriting a constant.

PARITY (this bead's Serial-vs-CpuMulti criterion): BITWISE IDENTICAL at 1/2/4/8 rayon workers on a deliberately imbalanced 2048-lane batch, for Brent, bisection, Newton and the cubic kernel -- every observable field (iterate, residual, bracket width, iteration count, status) compared via to_bits(). This is easier here than for ldu_matrix because a root batch has no cross-lane arithmetic and therefore no association to perturb. One documented caveat the module cannot defend against: a caller closure that is not a pure function of (i, x) breaks it.

Thread scaling, 65536 imbalanced lanes: serial 19322.52 us; 1 worker 0.94x, 2 workers 1.91x, 4 workers 2.73x (3.66x on the repeat), 8 workers 2.64x (3.57x). No gain past core count -- the compute-bound signature, in contrast to the superlinear >3x seen on 4 cores for SpMV.

ANALYTIC-ORACLE V&V: cubic roots 1/2/3 recovered EXACTLY (0.000000e0 error) by bisection, Brent and Newton. Worst |x - sqrt(k)| over 64 lanes: 1.776357e-15 (Brent), 8.881784e-16 (Newton). Mean iterations 7.73 Newton vs 13.14 Brent. Cubic batch worst residual 3.979039e-13 over 12288 real roots, worst root displacement 2.079981e-10 (near-coincident random root triples -- ill-conditioning, documented). Quadratic worst residual 7.105427e-15.

Serial-vs-Gpu parity remains ENTIRELY OPEN for this module: no GPU kernel, Gpu degrades to the best CPU path.

CAVEATS: one machine, 4 cores, idle, two runs. Not measured on Android/Termux or a many-core server. POLY_ROOTS_MIN_EQUATIONS was measured with CUBICS ONLY; quadratic and linear are cheaper per lane so they cross over later and inherit the floor as an assumption. POLY_BLOCK=256 is a granularity floor that was not swept, only verified not to change a value.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
END-TO-END SOLVER SPEED-UP, MEASURED at last — 2026-08-13. This is the first evidence in epic op-yvj.4 that any of it makes a REAL SOLVE faster; everything before this was micro-benchmarks. Fifth independent run, available_parallelism()=4, /proc/loadavg 1.53 0.85 0.37 rising to 1.67 1.00 0.45, best of 5. Asymmetric 7-point stencil.

  cells     Jacobi ser->par (ms)    speedup    ILU(0) ser->par (ms)    speedup
  4096      12.675 -> 18.785        0.67x LOSS  6.658 -> 11.075        0.60x LOSS
  32768     104.810 -> 61.699       1.70x       54.984 -> 42.558       1.29x
  512000    2024.812 -> 815.677     2.48x       1013.883 -> 676.072    1.50x

*** THE KERNEL'S CROSSOVER IS NOT THE SOLVER'S CROSSOVER. *** At 4096 cells -- EXACTLY SPMV_MIN_CELLS, the constant this bead recorded as SpMV's measured break-even -- the full solve LOSES, in all five runs. The solve only starts winning around 13000 cells. A kernel threshold measured in isolation does not transfer to the consumer that calls it, because the consumer also pays for the vector operations, the preconditioner and the residual bookkeeping, each with its own scaling. This is the most actionable thing on this bead: per-kernel constants are necessary but NOT sufficient, and a caller needs its own crossover.

ILU(0) IS THE BRAKE, quantified rather than asserted. Both phases have loop-carried dependence and are not parallelised. Triangular solves are 29-46% of serial solve time (four runs: 34.1 / 37.4 / 37.3 / 40.7%), which by Amdahl caps attainable speed-up at 1.7-2.1x on 4 cores. Measured 1.50x sits BELOW that cap, so ILU(0) dominates but is not the only limit. Factorisation costs a further 23.8% of one serial solve per coefficient update.

REDUCTION-ORDER SAFETY, now measured instead of argued. The concern recorded earlier on this bead was that ldu_matrix::parallel's blocked dot is not bit-equal to krylov::vecops' flat sum (worst 2.3744e-13) and could flip an iteration count near a convergence tolerance. Swept 216 solve pairs -- 3 sizes x 3 dominances x 3 seeds x 4 tolerances (1e-6 to 1e-12) x 2 solvers: ZERO iteration-count flips. GMRES was included and had never been compared before; it is the more exposed solver, with roughly 4x the reductions per iteration and a stopping test that reads a Givens recurrence rather than a fresh norm. Max relative residual difference 2.220e-4, which sounds alarming but is an ABSOLUTE difference of ~1.9e-16 on a residual of 8.6e-13. The BiCGStab worst case stopped at 0.86x its own tolerance -- about as near the deciding boundary as the grid reaches -- and still did not flip. Zero flips in 216 pairs bounds the rate at roughly 1-in-216 for systems of this kind; it is NOT proof that no system flips.

Serial vs CpuMulti is BIT-EXACT for both solvers including every residual-history entry, not merely the final answer.

TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS the agent made from its own printed output, worth recording because they are the failure mode this epic keeps hitting: a predecessor's claim that 'GMRES gains less than BiCGStab at every size tested' is FALSE at 4096 cells, where GMRES was ahead (0.78x vs 0.67x) -- now restricted to >=32768 cells; and an uncomputed range '23.8-24.7% across four runs' had been written into preconditioner.rs and was replaced with the single figure actually paired.

CAVEATS: one virtualised 4-core host that never idles (bn daemon ~37% of a core); one matrix family; f64 CPU only. There is NO GPU kernel in this path at all, so nothing here speaks to ComputeBackend::Gpu and the Serial-vs-Gpu half of this bead remains entirely open. Absolute milliseconds are not comparable across sessions -- serial times shifted ~2x between container restarts at LOWER load -- so only ratios should be read.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Closed as GitHub #16. Gate exists, runs, and has real numbers.

Parity: tests/hybrid_parity.rs — an integration test, so it sees only the public surface. gate_parity_serial_vs_cpu_multi / _vs_gpu compare bitwise (f64::to_bits) for kernels claiming bitwise identity and by stated tolerance for those that legitimately re-associate, with the class recorded per kernel in ParityClass so the two cannot be confused. New gate_gpu_kernels_match_the_oracle covers the WGSL kernels that now exist.

The tripwire gate_gpu_degrades_and_does_not_lie changed meaning and the change is documented: it used to assert 'no module reports Gpu BECAUSE no GPU kernel exists'. Real kernels exist now, so it asserts the narrower, deliberate policy that no module AUTO-SELECTS Gpu.

Benchmarks: examples/hybrid_gpu_report.rs, sweeping 4096..4194304 lanes, timing all three backends including host-device transfer. Result: the GPU never won, losing to CpuMulti by 5x-100x at every size. Per this bead's own guidance that is a legitimate result, written down rather than shipped as a slower default — every GPU kernel is off auto-select.

METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION worth keeping: the harness's first version reported deviations of exactly 0.00e0 for four of five kernels. That was not a good result — the test data were dyadic fractions, exactly representable in f32, so the comparison measured nothing. Non-dyadic inputs are now used and are what make the figures real. Anyone re-running this must preserve that property.

Caveat on the crossover conclusion: the only usable adapter was an Intel iGPU on the OpenGL backend against 32 CPU threads (the box's RTX A5000 had no kernel driver loaded). Re-running on a working discrete GPU is the obvious next measurement.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: CPU-vs-GPU parity gates + crossover benchmarks for the hybrid math kernels
